articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft dropped 167 patches including a SharePoint zero-day and Windows Defender's 'BlueHammer' flaw, while Chrome patched its fourth zero-day this year. April showers bring May flowers, and apparently they also bring security nightmares.

articles.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: Linux Rootkit, macOS Crypto Stealer, WebSocket Skimmers and More
articles.summary: Google spotted the first AI-developed zero-day exploit in the wild—a 2FA bypass no less. The machines aren't just coming for our jobs, they're debugging their way into our accounts.

articles.title: Hackers Used AI to Develop First Known Zero-Day 2FA Bypass for Mass Exploitation
articles.summary: CVE-2026-41940 in cPanel is getting hammered by Mr_Rot13 (love the handle) to drop Filemanager backdoors. When your web hosting control panel becomes someone else's control panel.

articles.title: Canada’s Bill C-22 Is a Repackaged Version of Last Year’s Surveillance Nightmare
articles.summary: Russian military intelligence turned old routers into Microsoft Office token vending machines. Your grandmother's Linksys just became a foreign intelligence asset.

articles.title: Anti-DDoS Firm Heaped Attacks on Brazilian ISPs
articles.summary: Canvas got pwned during finals week because apparently cybercriminals have no chill. Millions of students nationwide couldn't access coursework while hackers held their education hostage.

articles.title: Ollama Out-of-Bounds Read Vulnerability Allows Remote Process Memory Leak
articles.summary: NVIDIA's GeForce NOW leaked Armenian user data because even GPU giants can't escape the breach industrial complex. Cloud gaming, cloud crying.

articles.title: Big Finance Might Be Dooming the SPLC — Even Before Its Day in Court
articles.summary: The DOJ now treats dodging FOIA requests as criminal behavior worthy of arrest—rich coming from the same administration that perfected government transparency theater. Rules for thee, not for me.

articles.title: EFF Stands in Solidarity With RightsCon and the Global Digital Rights Community
articles.summary: EFF argues border device searches need warrants because the Fourth Amendment didn't come with a 'customs exception' asterisk. Your phone's constitutional rights shouldn't end at the airport.

articles.title: EFF to Fourth Circuit: Electronic Device Searches at the Border Require a Warrant
articles.summary: Canada repackaged last year's surveillance nightmare as Bill C-22, proving that bad privacy legislation is like herpes—it always comes back. Democracy dies in rebranding.

articles.title: Native Apps Should Be Avoided Whenever Possible
articles.summary: LLMs killed the 90-day disclosure window by making exploit development instant—the security researcher's lament that responsible disclosure just got a lot less responsible. Welcome to the age of AI-accelerated pwning.
